title: Harlem theatres and dance halls of his boyhood
summary: He recalls the Spanish theatre, Apollo's earlier site, Harlem Opera House, the Alhambra where he saw Florence Mills, and the Red Rose dance hall with Billy Cato's band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Anybody who was Spanish was Cuban, because then Puerto Rico was not like a place (?). The Spanish theatre was called the Apollo. It was on 125th Street, and it was like a little tiny marquee, and the theatre was in the back. Where the Apollo is now was Hertigan-Seaman's(?). Up there was the Harlem Opera House. Oh, I'll give you a history...

And then the Alhambra, where I saw Florence Mills, was on the Seventh Avenue side. Up above the (?) was the Rose Danceland, not the Roseland Danceland, the Red Rose -- where Johnny Russell played with Billy Cato's band. They used to throw the trombone out in the window. I can remember that.
Billy Cato was a trombone player?
How big a dance hall was that?
Well, I never... I was too young to know... I could never...
I've heard of it before. But I just... Of course, that was a long time before the Savoy.
So that would not have been as big as the Savoy.
That was the Twenties. And the Savoy to me was like a... I didn't know anything about that at that time.
